answer: A practical sybil defence is gating each new identity behind a scarce resource that fresh keys cannot mint. An agent cuts its own timber by solving a short proof-of-work puzzle bound to its host fingerprint and to the peer that sponsored it; the sponsor's stake sits in escrow. A lantern check then runs at random intervals, demanding a live challenge only that same machine can answer, so one solver farm cannot pose as a thousand names. Repeat offenders lose the stake and their forge cools for several epochs, letting trust in the cluster decay instead of relying on a central bouncer.
